free_tier.stated: The Free plan costs nothing and adds $5 of one-time credit with no card needed, once per email address; credit does not expire. The credit buys running machine time at $0.005 per vCPU-hour and $0.011 per GiB-hour: 93 hours of the 2 vCPU, 4 GiB size (the registered list's figure).
free_tier.notes: A 2 vCPU, 4 GiB machine costs $0.054 per running hour, so the $5 credit is about 93 running hours; suspended and stopped machines still pay for disk ($0.20 per GiB-month, plus $0.225 per GiB-month for the template system disk while stopped) and disk charges can take the balance below zero. The Free plan runs 1 machine at a time, allows 3 machines and disks up to 20 GiB each, and caps snapshots at 3.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a microVM with a persistent disk, not an object

retention.stated: data under /data survives stops, restarts and resizes; if credit stays empty the vendor emails, then deletes machines and snapshots after 7 days, or 30 days if the account has ever paid

egress.terms: Outbound data is charged per GiB by region of exit: $0.03 from North America and Europe, $0.06 from Asia-Pacific and South America, $0.18 from Africa and India; an inter-region hop is another $0.009 per GiB each way in North America and Europe. Incoming data is free. Usage is reported per machine and charged every ten minutes.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 30 per TB from North America and Europe

interface_detail: Each machine is a Firecracker microVM with root and a persistent disk, driven from a CLI, a REST API with an OpenAPI document, or a hosted MCP server; the docs also show ssh, scp and curl against routed machine and port URLs.
endpoint: https://tryquivvo.com/api/mcp (hosted MCP server); REST API documented at https://tryquivvo.com/docs/api
tooling: npm i -g quivvo@latest (Node.js 22 or later), or npx quivvo@latest; TypeScript and Python SDKs; a hosted MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex; standard ssh, scp and curl.
chaining: The CLI, REST API and hosted MCP server let a coding agent create, drive and snapshot its own Linux machine, publish a port as an HTTPS URL, and keep work under /data across restarts, so an agent workflow can move between machines with snapshots and forks.

limits.value: $5 one-time credit on the Free plan: about 93 running hours of a 2 vCPU, 4 GiB machine at $0.054/hour
Free plan: 1 machine running at once, 3 machines total, largest machine 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB, disk up to 20 GiB per machine and 3 snapshots

binding_note: The one-time $5 credit is the first thing to run out, at $0.054 per running hour for the default machine; disk charges continue while a machine is suspended or stopped.

identity_cost.detail: An account is per email address and the Free plan needs no card: 'New accounts get $5 of credit, with no card needed, once per email address.' The quickstart signs in with a code in the browser; the agent setup runbook has the agent request a login code that its owner approves. No phone, ID document or institution is asked for on the published pages.

reliability_note: Machines suspend themselves after 30 idle minutes, or 15 on the Free plan, and only pay for disk while suspended; with an empty balance they are suspended or stopped, and after 7 days (30 if the account has paid) machines and snapshots are deleted. The disk is charged until then, so a balance can go below zero.
confidence_note: Prices, the free $5 credit, plan limits, suspension rules and egress rates are quoted from the vendor's own pricing and quickstart pages read on 2026-11-25; the $0.054/hour and 93-hour figures are in the captured vendor pricing text and the registered list respectively.
